clue.text: With arm on the counter, obtains fast food

indicators.note: read against the normal direction, so the word for an arm is turned round

parts.note: a gun is an arm, a weapon
obtains means gets

explanation.surface: Someone leaning an elbow on a shop counter while picking up a quick takeaway meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like the limb on the counter, but it is a weapon: GUN, read backwards as NUG, then GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken nuggets are a staple item on the menus of quick-service burger chains.

clue.text: Hot Señoritas dancing in Russian republic

indicators.note: the letters jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: Sultry Spanish women dancing somewhere in the Caucasus.
explanation.definitionFit: North Ossetia–Alania is a federal subject of Russia in the North Caucasus.

clue.text: Demanding porridge with fish

parts.note: gruel is thin porridge
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Insisting on oats and a fish for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demanding' looks like a verb in the surface but is the adjective meaning exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruelling work is exhausting and taxing, as is demanding work.

clue.text: Went public with shocks, essentially all at the same time

indicators.note: the essence is the core, so the central letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A company floated on the stock market amid surprises.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles of Went, public and shocks are EN, BL and OC.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is a French phrase meaning as a whole, all together in one go.

clue.text: Frightened and traumatised, one runs away

indicators.note: away says the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: someone traumatised is emotionally scarred
R is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for runs; 'one' means just a single R goes

explanation.surface: A terrified, shaken person flees.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARRED has two Rs; only one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared is a straightforward synonym for afraid or frightened.

clue.text: Players nearly dispossess left-winger

parts.note: the players in a production are its cast

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, its final letter cut off

parts.note: to dispossess someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: A football-style picture of a team almost stealing the ball from a winger on the left flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-winger' suggests a footballer, but it is a political leftist: Fidel Castro, the Cuban revolutionary leader. ROB loses its last letter to give RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Cuba's communist revolution, a figure of the political left.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment of Buzz Aldrin?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a perforated bowl for draining food
second, punning meaning: Buzz Aldrin was a USAF colonel (Col.) and flew the Apollo 11 lunar lander, so a 'Col. Lander'

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: COL is the abbreviation for colonel and Aldrin piloted the lander.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a bowl with holes used for straining pasta or vegetables.

clue.text: Lack of transportation in South London?

indicators.note: the vehicle sits inside the other letters

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
the City is London's financial district; the question mark marks it as one example
a car is a means of transportation

explanation.surface: A complaint about poor transport links south of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity is a shortage or insufficiency of something.

clue.text: Hurried Federer finally hit an unreturnable serve

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the tennis player's surname

parts.note: to ace an opponent is to serve a ball they cannot touch

explanation.surface: Roger Federer quickly finished a match with an ace.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced means rushed or moved at speed.

clue.text: Imaginary line originally ran halfway under Mont Blanc

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: A route or border that once ran partway beneath the Alps' highest mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of ran, halfway, under, Mont and Blanc spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhumb line is a navigational course crossing every meridian at the same angle, drawn on charts but not physically present.

clue.text: Agreement in romantic relationship beginning to disappear

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is to vanish

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual romantic affair

explanation.surface: A pact found within a love affair that is starting to fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: DALLIANCE loses its first letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a pact or union formed between parties for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Creator of life is outspoken scientific genius, I conceded

parts.note: frank means candid, outspoken

indicators.note: conceded in the sense of given up, so the letter is surrendered

parts.note: Albert Einstein, the physicist
the letter I

explanation.surface: A boastful scientist admits he is the genius behind life itself.
explanation.walkthrough: EINSTEIN gives up its first I to leave ENSTEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Frankenstein in Mary Shelley's novel brings a creature to life.

clue.text: Let European into type of party that's celebrated in fancy dress

indicators.note: the letters go inside the word for the party

parts.note: a hen party is a celebration for a bride before her wedding
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: An invitation to admit someone from Europe to a costume party.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party (British for a bachelorette party) wraps ALLOW plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: On 31 October people dress up in costumes as witches, ghosts and monsters for trick-or-treating and parties.

clue.text: Investigators meeting queen for drink

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the Queen

explanation.surface: Police detectives sharing a drink with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic beverage fermented from apple juice.

clue.text: Hard to stop lust, perhaps, showing a bit of leg

indicators.note: the letter plugs the word, sitting inside it as a stopper does

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins, hence 'perhaps'
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A struggle to curb desire when someone flashes a glimpse of leg.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside SIN; lust is given as an example of a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: The shin is the front part of the lower leg below the knee.

clue.text: Check balance, then shower

parts.note: the balance or remainder is the rest
a shower is a spell of rain

explanation.surface: A bathroom routine: weigh yourself on the scales, then step into the shower.
explanation.definitionFit: To check someone or something is to hold it back or curb it.

clue.text: Deeply regrets going naked to cuddle inspirational figure for fun

indicators.note: the outer letters wrap round, hugging the other word
stripped bare, losing its outer letters

parts.note: to lament is to mourn or deeply regret
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: Someone full of regret strips off and hugs their muse for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going naked' reads as the person stripping, but it strips the word of its outer letters, leaving AMENT to hug the muse.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is entertainment or enjoyment, a synonym for fun.

clue.text: Deluded elite marksman, one quietly replaced by another

indicators.note: replaced by signals swapping the first letters out for the second

parts.note: a crack shot is an expert marksman
SH is one way of asking for quiet
P, for piano, is another musical sign for quietly

explanation.surface: A deranged sniper whose silent partner is swapped for someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words for quiet: SH out, P (piano, in music) in.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot as an adjective describes eccentric, impractical or crazy ideas or people.

clue.text: Record that crime is overwhelming Northern worker

indicators.note: overwhelming as engulfing, so the crime surrounds the record

parts.note: a felony is a serious crime
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A record-breaking crime wave swamps a labourer in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fell pony is a hardy working breed from the Cumbrian fells of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell ponies were bred as pack and draught animals in northern England, so a worker.

clue.text: Bloated and drunk, need grog

indicators.note: being drunk leaves the letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swollen and tipsy craving another tot of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Grog is rum diluted with water, the old navy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Engorged means swollen, distended with fluid, so it fits being puffed up.

clue.text: This drug doesn't work, man

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A frustrated complaint that some medicine is useless, addressed to a mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' reads as an exclamation in the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude is American slang for a guy or fellow.

clue.text: Went to capture ancient city, but beaten to a pulp

indicators.note: capturing means taking in, so the city sits inside

parts.note: 'went' is a euphemism for urinated, peed
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An army set out to take a historic city but was crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' reads as travelled, but is the euphemism for went to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been puréed has been mashed or blended to a smooth paste.

clue.text: Recommendation of American director with immoral habit

parts.note: a vice is a wicked or immoral habit

explanation.surface: A reference letter for a US filmmaker with a dodgy lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance or a suggestion on what someone should do.

clue.text: Main dictionary describes several languages

indicators.note: describes in the sense of drawing a line round, enclosing the letters within the words

explanation.surface: A principal reference book that covers a number of tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: Indic is the branch of Indo-European including Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi and other tongues of India.

clue.text: Knock back doctor in nursing academy

indicators.note: nursing in the sense of holding close, so the letters cradle another

explanation.surface: A physician working at a nursing school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' looks like the profession taught at the academy; it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock back or drain a drink is to drink it down in one.

clue.text: The French take clothes off for someone to clean them

parts.note: la is a French word for 'the'
to take one's clothes off is to undress

explanation.surface: Stripping garments so a cleaner can wash them.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman employed to wash and iron garments.

clue.text: Child's pouch found in rubbish dump by Swede on vacation

parts.note: pap is worthless or trivial material
a dump is slang for a bowel movement, poo

indicators.note: emptied of its inside, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A baby carrier discovered at a tip by a Swedish visitor away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dump' looks like the rubbish tip, but it pairs with 'rubbish' as two pieces. PAPPOOSE is a recognised variant spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a bag or sling for carrying an infant on the back or chest.

clue.text: Girl's fair-trade candle regularly used

indicators.note: every third letter of the phrase is taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A young woman's ethically sourced candle.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every third letter (I, R, E, N, E) of 'fair-trade candle' spells the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Section of coursework not typically extremely difficult

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a student's assignment is unusually hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is one that is tangled and hard to solve.

clue.text: Thought a lot about smut-free retrospective

indicators.note: looking back, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: something free of smut is not lewd

explanation.surface: A clean-living look back over past work, considered at length.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT LEWD read backwards gives DWELT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dwelt on something is to have pondered or brooded over it.
